Independent Python Fraction evaluation of the first three logarithmic canonical coefficients from the two geometric PGFs
correctness.rationale: Summing the two geometric series gives poles q and q² and numerator factor 1−ρz; the mass is positive even at α=−1. The range −q≤ρ<q² yields nonnegative absolutely summable log coefficients, proving compound Poisson. To check the canonical criterion independently, write L=log G and b(z)=(z−1)L′(z); its coefficients from degree one on are a_k−a_{k+1}. The remainder PGF G(z)/G(1−c+cz) equals 1 at c=1, and its derivative with respect to 1−c there is b, so the differences must be nonnegative. Conversely log of that quotient is the integral from c to 1 of b(1−t+tz)/t; if the differences are nonnegative, b is a compound-Poisson exponent and the integral is another such exponent by binomial expansion. For ρ≥0, after dividing d_k by q^k the positive term m_k satisfies m_{k+1}−q m_k=(1−q)² and ρ/q<q; this propagates d_2≥0. For ρ=−s the odd differences are positive and the even-step comparison follows from increasing ratios of m_j=(1−q)+(1−q²)q^{2j}. The displayed factorization for m_2−m_1² is correct, with strict positivity from min(1−2q+2q³)=1−4/(3√3)>0. Thus m_j≥m_1^j≥(1+s)((s/q)²)^j whenever d_2≥0. Poisson changes only the first difference. Independent exact fractions reproduce both threshold witnesses and the four D_2 signs −,+,−,+ with λ+D_1>0 at q=99/100. Strict signs and continuity suffice for reentrance.
residual_risks: The rational witnesses are checks of particular parameters; the infinite criterion is proved analytically.

value.rationale: The finite sharp test for a previously specified count model replaces infinitely many constraints and also decides exactly whether an independent Poisson addition can rescue the property. The strict alternating witnesses refute an interval hypothesis within a family that remains compound Poisson. The all-index cutoff, not merely the log-coefficient calculation or an isolated rational example, is the substantive result.
residual_risks: No complete classification of all connected components in joint parameter space is asserted.
